motion: This House, as an average person in a developed country, would lead a life heavily prioritising long term commitments (people, places, vocations, etc.) over heavily prioritising flexibility and keeping options open
This House prefers a world in which post-apartheid South Africa nationalised major firms, rather than pursuing policies that expanded Black private ownership
This House believes that neoliberalism has failed
infoslide: Neoliberalism is an ideology that rose to prominence during the 1980s. It emphasises free markets, deregulation, and increased global economic integration.

motion: This House supports the modern revival of the Monroe Doctrine
infoslide: The Monroe Doctrine (1823) asserts that any intervention by external powers in the politics of the Americas would be viewed as a potentially hostile act against the US. Its modern revival refers to recent efforts to reassert the US sphere of influence to counter the growing presence of other powers (e.g., China, Russia) in South America.

motion: This House opposes the development of AI systems to optimise for human influence
infoslide: Human influence refers to the ability of AI systems to exert influence over humans by mimicking human features and behaviours. Examples of this include strategic human-like bargaining, persuasion, and emotional engagement.

motion: This House regrets the use of drastic state interventions to address the COVID-19 pandemic (e.g., prolonged mass lockdowns, school closures, vaccine mandates)
This House opposes the use of historical and religious narratives as justification for modern territorial claims
This House believes that domestication* has done more harm than good for non-human animals
This House predicts that the developing world will become more, rather than less, democratic over the next decade
This House believes that the EU should adopt a significantly more aggressive foreign policy stance* in response to Russian hybrid warfare operations in Europe

This House opposes the use of user-specific algorithms to deliver on-demand content for entertainment (including but not limited to: the pipeline of short-form videos on TikTok or Instagram, personalised suggestions on YouTube or Netflix)
This House believes that it is in the interests of the American people for the US government to acquire golden shares in strategically important firms (e.g., NVIDIA, MP Materials, US Steel)
infoslide: A golden share is a single, unique, state-held share that grants the government special veto and approval powers over strategic corporate decisions (such as foreign ownership, technology transfer, or asset relocation). Golden shares are typically created and transferred to the government through legislative or executive action.

motion: This House opposes the popularisation of social justice speak
infoslide: "Social justice speak" refers to the growing use of academic and activist terms about structural oppression and social inequality in everyday conversations, outside academic or activist settings. Examples include, but are not limited to, terms like: “mansplaining,” “white privilege,” “microaggressions,” and “intersectionality.”

motion: This House believes that Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman's rise to power has been good for Saudi Arabia
This House, as the leadership of a major news organisation (e.g., The Economist, CBS, The Washington Post), would adopt moralised journalism as a stance
infoslide: "Moralised journalism" refers to media outlets taking an explicit moral or values-driven approach in their reporting. Such outlets would take a clear and consistent stance on the issues they cover. This may include coverage that emphasises moral outrage, the use of emotionally charged language, and links to broader social narratives.

motion: This House prefers a world where all religions prohibited visual depictions of the divine over a world where such depictions were central to all religions
This House believes that Bulgaria should adopt a progressive tax system
infoslide:
Bulgaria has a flat tax system, applying a uniform 10% income tax after meeting a minimum income threshold.
A progressive tax system is a taxation model in which the tax rate increases as taxable income increases.

motion: This House Believes That Trumpism is in the long-term interest of the Republican Party
infoslide: Trumpism is a populist ideology and style of politics that combines elements of nationalism, anti-establishment sentiments, isolationism and being "anti-woke". Politicians that adopt Trumpism are usually more aggressive and abrasive in their public advocacy.

motion: This House, as the Holy See, would adopt the "two-speed Church" policy
infoslide:
The Holy See is the central governing body of the Catholic Church (including the Pope).
The term "two-speed Church" refers to an approach within the Catholic Church in which local or regional churches determine doctrines and practices or adopt reforms at varying paces, depending on their context.

motion: This House Opposes the increased shift to subscription based business models
infoslide: Companies are increasingly adopting subscription models for selling their physical and digital products instead of solely relying on one-time sales. For example, physical products such as Oura smart ring, Tesla vehicles, and Peloton exercise bikes require monthly fees to unlock some or all features, while digital products such as Adobe Creative Cloud and Microsoft 365 have transitioned from one-time purchase to subscription-based access.

motion: This House Supports the shift away from the traditional left-right spectrum in the politics of major democracies
This House Would militarily intervene in Sudan
This House Believes that it is in the interest of the USA to significantly reduce the size and power of federal government agencies
This House Opposes the prominence of the trauma plot in media and art
infoslide: The term "trauma plot" refers to narratives centered on personal traumatic experiences such as violence or abuse, emphasising individual suffering. Examples include novels such as A Little Life, It Ends With Us, Perks of Being a Wallfower, TV series such as Euphoria and BoJack Horseman, and songs such as Billie Eilish’s "Bury A Friend".

motion: This House Supports the widespread adoption of the Sankofa philosophy in West Africa
infoslide: Sankofa is a Ghanaian philosophy that emphasises learning from the past to shape a better future. Embracing this philosophy may involve glorifying traditional practices through popular culture and art, supporting traditional livelihoods and ways of living (e.g., promoting rereruralisation, supporting industries such as breweries, agriculture, and fishing, etc), and teaching indigenous languages in schools.

motion: This House Believes that India should prioritise policies that aim to significantly reduce economic inequality rather than prioritise policies that aim to rapidly drive economic growth
This House Supports the use of La Mano Dura policies in areas with high crime rates in Latin America.
infoslide: La Mano Dura refers to tough-on-crime policies aimed at combating gang violence and organised crime. This approach is characterised by increased police operations and military involvement, harsher penalties for gang-related activities, and lowering the barriers for arrests.

motion: This House Prefers the citizen welfare standard to the consumer welfare standard
infoslide:
The consumer welfare standard is a legal doctrine that states that business conduct and mergers and acquisitions are only anti-competitive and should be prevented when they harm consumers (e.g., by raising prices, lowering quality, reducing innovation, etc.).
In contrast, the citizen welfare standard is a legal doctrine that states business conduct and mergers and acquisitions are to be evaluated on consumer and non-economic outcomes (e.g., privacy, environment, democracy, etc).

motion: This House Supports the rise of specialised private equity firms and funds that focus on specific sectors or geographies
This House Believes that the student organisers of the July Revolution should not transition into formal political roles (e.g., run for elected office, form their own political party)
infoslide: The July Revolution was a mass popular student-led uprising that ousted Bangladesh's ruling Awami League government and led to the establishment of a politically neutral interim government. The student organisers of the uprising have since occupied important positions within the interim government and founded the National Citizen's Committee (Jatiyo Nagorik Committee), a non-affiliated platform aimed at "building a democractic Bangladesh". Many of the student organisers were previously involved in political organising under the banners of various political parties.

motion: This House Believes that feminists in Western Liberal Democracies should adopt reconciliatory rather than confrontational approaches in their advocacy
This House Believes that US involvement in Panama has benefitted Panama
This House Opposes confidence culture
infoslide: Confidence culture places a high value on the development and expression of personal confidence. It emphasises the importance of self-assurance, self promotion, and assertiveness, framing these traits as critical to achieving individual goals.

motion: This House Prefers secondary schools adopting a classical education model rather than a progressive education model
infoslide:
Classical education relies on teacher-led, structured lectures, with minimal student driven discussion or exercises. Subjects are distinct units that are clearly delineated (e.g., math, English, etc) and taught primarily through textbooks.
In contrast, progressive education positions teachers as facilitators with a focus on student-led discussion, project-based learning, and experiential learning. Learning is organised thematically around a single topic (e.g., environmentalism, space exploration, etc) and can draw on sources such as news articles, fiction books, documentaries, and academic papers from different areas (science, history, etc.).
For the purpose of this debate, secondary schools refer to schools with students from age of 14 to 18.

motion: This House believes that post-revolutionary states should deemphasise the role of elite groups in favour of portraying revolution as primarily led by the lower classes
This House prefers a diverse number of highly competitive banks to a small number of banks.
This House welcomes the end of work
This House would ban defensive measures against hostile take overs.
infoslide: Defensive measures against hostile take overs include poison pills, a staggered board, and scorched earth policies.  Poison pills specify that if a single entity or person acquires a large enough stake, the company will issue shares.  All other shareholders become eligible to acquire those shares for a large discount or for free.  A staggered board is a board that consists of directors who serve terms of different lengths, making it difficult for an acquirer to replace the whole board quickly.  Scorched earth policies damage the company if a hostile take over is imminent, for example by selling assets at a discount.

motion: This House believes that religious leaders should primarily focus on individual circumstances rather than community-based reasons when addressing acts of religious extremism
infoslide: When dealing with religious extremism within the community, religious leaders can choose to focus on either community-based reasons (e.g. highlighting a lack of condemnation for extremism within the community, failure to address misinterpretations of religious texts, or inadequate efforts to promote tolerance and understanding among followers), or individual circumstances (e.g. highlighting factors like poverty, war-induced trauma, or mental health issues affecting the specific individuals involved in the attack).

motion: This House opposes the norm to prefer the natural to the artificial
This House would ban vulture funds from suing countries whose debt they have purchased.
infoslide: A vulture fund is fund that invests in sovereign debt that a government is refusing to pay back (distressed debt). It buys this debt from the original debt holder at a discount, and then aggressively pursues (often through litigation) the government to pay off the debt at a higher price than what the vulture fund purchased the debt for.

motion: This House supports implementing a Pact of Forgetting in post-conflict states
infoslide: A Pact of Forgetting is a political agreement after the fall of a dictatorship.  The pact is made between major political parties to avoid directly confronting the legacy of a dictatorship and the conflict which brought it to an end.  It includes not prosecuting members of a former regime and agreeing to not commemorate any actions of that regime, and instead concentrating on the future.  An example of this is the agreement in Spain between Franco-aligned right wing parties and new left wing parties after the end of Franco’s regime.

motion: This House opposes the stigma against laziness
This House would remove restrictions on interstate farm commerce in India.
infoslide: Domestic agriculture in India is regulated by individual states, which establish local auction markets (mandis) within their borders. Farmers are required to sell their produce via auction only at the mandi in their locality, and purchasers (wholesalers, exporters, retail traders) must also be from that region. There are then steep tariffs for re-selling produce across states borders.

motion: This House supports a norm against self-pity.
THBT central banks should 'lean against the wind'.
infoslide: "Leaning against the wind" is a policy employed by some central banks to explicitly target financial stability (e.g., avoiding asset price bubbles and credit booms) by setting higher interest rates during periods of economic growth. This is distinct from the philosophy of most Western central banks, which exclusively consider inflation and unemployment (e.g., by maintaining a target inflation rate).

motion: This House supports Centrist Compacts.
infoslide: A Centrist Compact is an agreement between major political parties. The Centrist Compact applies where one of the major parties is able to form a government after an election with the support of a minor party. In such a case, the other major party will provide it the minimum number of votes necessary to govern without the support of the minor party. A Centrist Compact is not legally binding.

motion: This House prefers reactive to proactive EMS enforcement
infoslide: Environmental managements systems (EMS) are the laws and regulations which govern land use, water use, and pollution.  Proactive EMS enforcement requires people and companies to apply for permission before acting (ie, you need to apply for approval to build a house). Reactive EMS enforcement allows people or companies to act immediately, and then severely punishes those who breach the laws or regulations (ie, you incur a large fine if your house is too tall, or if it has not been checked by a certified engineer).

motion: This House supports the remilitarisation of Japan.
This House believes that opposition parties in illiberal democracies should strongly pivot towards empowering women as the primary focus of their campaign.
This House prefers the integrated model to the specialty model
infoslide: There are two ways that governments can consider disadvantage in policy-making. The "integrated model" incorporates disadvantage as an inherent consideration in policy-making (e.g. all new policies made in the education department must consider implications for rural students). The "specialty model" involves having a distinct division that specifically engages with policy for disadvantaged groups (e.g. the education department has a division that directly and separately addresses helping rural areas).

motion: This House believes that education systems should over-inflate children’s academic self-perception (e.g. providing overwhelmingly positive feedback, avoiding fail grades, etc.).
THBT religious organisations should syncretise over remaining independent
infoslide: Religious Syncretism is the practice of blending cultural/religious indigenous practices with different religious beliefs (for example, the Catholic Church merging traditional saints with local deities in Latin America). Religious Independence is the belief that one's religion must remain tied to a unique set of religious teachings that contain the truth about humanity and divinity.

motion: THBT education systems in Africa should emphasise pan-African history and identities rather than national ones
THBT the IMF removing all conditions on these loans, except for explicit anti corruption provisions, is preferable to the recent conditions to developing countries
infoslide: During the recent economic crisis, the International Monetary Fund (IMF) has provided certain conditions to developing countries for receiving loans. These conditions require governments to adopt more market based economic policies. Targets include reducing government budget deficits and increasing international currency reserves. The policy conditions provided by the IMF include 1) reducing or eliminating fuel subsidies and fertiliser subsidies; 2) setting the currency exchange rate to international market rates; 3) implementing market-based interest rates; 4) anti corruption provisions.

motion: THW allow democratic governments to overturn supreme court/constitutional court decisions with a simple majority in the legislature
THBT the internationalisation of intellectual property law brings more harm than good
infoslide:
Intellectual property is a category of property that includes ‘intangible’ creations of human intellect. There are many types of intellectual property including patents, copyrights and trademarks.
The ‘internationalisation’ of intellectual property law refers to efforts to make intellectual property rights universally applicable, including the widespread use of treaties to recognise intellectual property rights across different jurisdictions, the creation of the World Intellectual Property Organisation, etc.

motion: THBT it is in the interests of Taiwan to pursue friendlier ties with China (e.g. economic, political and cultural ties)
THBT governments, when determining housing policy, should heavily prioritise supporting renters over home owners
THBT The Pacific Alliance should introduce a common currency
infoslide: The Pacific Alliance (Spanish: Alianza del Pacífico) is a Latin American trade bloc, formed by Chile, Colombia, Mexico and Peru.

motion: THBT it's in the interest of the team for the player to be excluded from the World Cup finals squad
infoslide: A team that’s recently gained prominence after great performances at the World Cup has advanced to World Cup finals for the first time. After the semi final, the team's top scorer and most important player, while drunk at a bar, publicly instigated a physical fight against another member of the team. When asked to calm down they continued to double down, causing more of a public disruption and seemingly irreconcilable differences with other members of the team.

motion: This House Believes That American frontier AI firms* should cease all cooperation with the US military.
This House Regrets the cultural dominance of sport.
This House Prefers market-based systems over bank-based systems.
infoslide:
In a market-based system (e.g. the US and UK), firms raise most external finance directly from private investors via stock and bond markets.
In a bank-based system (e.g. Germany and Japan), firms rely on long-term relationships with commercial banks for credit.
Under a market-based system, shareholders monitor the management and governance of the firm; under a bank-based system, the bank does so.

motion: This House, as the government of the UAE, Regrets its pivot away from Saudi Arabia.
infoslide: In recent years, the United Arab Emirates' foreign policy has increasingly diverged from the foreign policy of Saudi Arabia. The UAE has recently left OPEC, independently deepened its security ties with the United States and Israel, and taken an aggressive stance on Iran (which contrasts with Saudi Arabia's pursuit of détente with Iran). The UAE has also increased its unilateral involvement in military conflicts in the region, including military interventions and support for armed forces in Libya, Egypt, Yemen, Sudan, and the Horn of Africa.

motion: This House Regrets the centrality of individual redemption* to religions.
This House Believes That LGBTQ+ Pride month* does more harm than good.
This House Opposes the belief that loyalty is a virtue.
This House Prefers the institutional model to the project model for the public funding of research.
infoslide:
Institutional funding for public research is government funding given directly to universities and public research institutions as stable, long-term grants. Institutions have autonomy to decide their research priorities.
Project funding, by contrast, involves funding agencies awarding grants for projects through competitive processes. Researchers are required to submit grant proposals that outline specific objectives, timelines, and deliverables.
Other academic purposes, such as teaching, are funded separately.

motion: This House Believes That Andy Burnham should call an immediate general election.
This House Believes That psychiatric deinstitutionalisation did more harm than good.
infoslide: Psychiatric deinstitutionalisation was the shift in the 1950s-60s away from housing and treating people with mental illnesses in large long-term psychiatric institutions and toward treatment in community-based settings (e.g. at home, outpatient clinics, general practitioners).

motion: This House Hopes for the rise of energy-intensive facilities that use behind-the-meter generation in the European Union.
infoslide:
Behind-the-meter generation, also known as “off grid” generation, is a form of private, independent energy generation.
In the United States, energy-intensive facilities (e.g. data centres and factories) are often equipped with private, on-site power plants which are powered by gas, green energy with batteries, or mini nuclear reactors. The power plants remain independent of the public energy grid; some may, however, keep a limited connection for backup or to sell surplus power.

motion: This House Prefers art that depicts societal tragedies through allegories (The Yellow Wallpaper, Animal Farm, The Platform) over art that depicts societal tragedies explicitly (Schindler's List, Apocalypse Now, 12 Years a Slave).
This House, as Western governments, Regrets their support for Kosovo independence after the 1999 NATO intervention.
infoslide:
From 1945 to 1990, Kosovo was an autonomous region within Serbia, which was part of Yugoslavia. Most of Kosovo is ethnically Albanian and follows Islam.
In 1999, NATO intervened in Serbia on humanitarian grounds to protect the Kosovo Albanian population. Following this, Serbia's police and military forces left the region.
In 2008, Kosovo unilaterally declared independence with extensive political and economic support from the West. Today, Kosovo is recognised by around half of all UN Member States, including most of the EU and NATO. Notable countries that do not recognise Kosovo include Serbia and the five founding BRICS states.

motion: This House Prefers the Dutch Model over the Nordic Model.
infoslide:
Under the “Dutch Model” for sex work, both buying and selling sex are legal. Licensed brothels, escort services, and independent prostitution are allowed and regulated as a form of labour.
Under the “Nordic Model” for sex work, selling sex is generally legal, but buying sex is illegal. Brothels and third-party facilitation of prostitution are also illegal.

motion: This House Believes That the digitisation of the illegal drug trade* does more harm than good.
This House Supports the expectation that our loved ones accept us as we are.
This House Believes That humanity should implement the Prime Directive.
infoslide:
In the distant future, humanity has developed the capability to travel to distant worlds. In doing so it has encountered many civilisations (of intelligent extraterrestrial life), and continues to do so.
The Prime Directive is a general instruction of non-intervention. It states that, when humans interact with less developed civilisations, those humans should not seek to alter the social, cultural or technological development of the civilisation.
This includes but is not limited to: prohibitions on providing less developed civilisations with advanced technologies or medicines; making no references to the existence of other extraterrestrial life forms and civilisations; not intervening against leaders that humanity deems morally dubious.

motion: This House Believes That the World Bank should lend African development loans in ADR.
infoslide: For the purposes of this debate, African Drawing Rights (ADR) is a currency unit (or currency basket) whose value is calculated as a weighted average of five African currencies: 40% South African Rand, 25% Egyptian Pound, 15% Nigerian Naira, 10% Central African CFA Franc, and 10% West African CFA Franc. The worth of 1 ADR depends on how strong or weak these five African currencies are.

motion: This House Opposes the expectation that a person must 'grow up' (e.g. stigmatisation of childishness, outgrowing childhood friendships and relationships, moving on from childhood interests).
This House Believes That capitalism enhances our sense of meaning in life.
This House Believes That the United Nations should establish an international criminal tribunal for the events of the Syrian Civil War.
This House Prefers a World where religious closeness is dominant, as opposed to a world where religious distance is dominant.
infoslide:
Religious closeness is the belief that God is everywhere and in everything. It preaches that individuals should consider the divine implications of their daily actions (e.g. cooking, gardening, work, etc.) and act as if they are doing them for God and in the name of God.
Religious distance is the belief that God is distant from the world. It preaches that individuals can only find God by religious practices (s.a. praying, meditating, giving offers, etc.) and should only be contacted for significant decisions (e.g. choosing who to marry, dodging the draft, etc.).

motion: This House Supports European universities limiting freedom of speech among their staff and students.
This House Regrets the decline in Western military interventions following the 2003 Iraq War.
This House Predicts that in 10 years the majority of the world's population will consider the creation of generative AI to have been a mistake.
This House Prefers a World where the LGBTQ+ movement pursued the liberationist approach rather than the assimilationist approach.
infoslide:
Since the 1990s, the assimilationist approach to LGBTQ+ advocacy emphasised that queer identity and relationships are "just like" their heterosexual counterparts, and that therefore LGBTQ+ people should have access to existing social institutions such as marriage and family life.
The liberationist approach to LGBTQ+ advocacy would have argued that these institutions are inherently restrictive and should not be central to a person's life.

motion: This House Believes That the CDU should heavily prioritise libertarianism rather than heavily prioritising paternalism.
infoslide:
Libertarianism is a political philosophy that emphasises individual liberty and autonomy. It seeks to limit state intervention in influencing individual's behaviour, avoid intervening in economic markets, and limit government spending.
Paternalism, by contrast, argues that the state has a responsibility to direct society towards desirable goals. It argues that the state should have an active role in guiding individual behaviour, supports market intervention when deemed necessary, and supports comparatively higher government spending.
The Christian Democratic Union (CDU) is a historically dominant centre-right party in Germany. The party has both paternalistic and libertarian positions.

motion: This House Prefers a World in which all football clubs follow the regional recruitment model.
infoslide: Under a regional recruitment model, professional football clubs only sign players who are either born in their region or spent a significant portion of their life there. For example, Athletic Bilbao in Spain only signs players who were born in or lived significant part of their lives in the Basque region.

motion: This House Opposes the narrative that doctors know best.
This House Prefers a World where a more optimistic set of artists rose to prominence after World War I rather than the Lost Generation.
infoslide:
For the purposes of this debate, the Lost Generation is a group of writers and artists who created their art in and around World War I (e.g. writers such as Ernest Hemingway, Virginia Woolf, F. Scott Fitzgerald; other artists such as Edvard Munch and Otto Dix).
The art of the Lost Generation featured prominent themes of disillusionment, defeatism, and uncertainty about the future. The artists often drew from their experience of the war and their troubled personal lives. Their art has had significant influence over later artistic trends and holds a prominent position in many art and literature curriculums globally.

motion: This House Believes That Denmark should aggressively intervene in the private sector in order to reduce dependence on Novo Nordisk (e.g. dramatically reduce existing subsidies to Novo Nordisk; implement state-backed retraining programmes; provide large targeted tax breaks to startups in non-dominant industries like green tech).
infoslide: Novo Nordisk is a multinational pharmaceutical company from Denmark which specialises in diabetes medication. It is known for discovering and manufacturing the drug behind Ozempic. Novo Nordisk represents approximately 20% of Denmark's stock market and is the most significant company in the Danish economy.

motion: This House Opposes the widespread belief that people who have committed violent crimes are inherently irredeemable.
THBT the Old Firm should join the English Football league structure, rather than stay in the Scottish Premiership.
infoslide:
Celtic and Rangers (collectively referred to as 'The Old Firm') are the two largest football clubs in Scotland and currently play in the Scottish Premiership. 'The Old Firm' has been dominating the Scottish Premiership, and the number of attendees at their home games are equal to the rest of the top two divisions of Scottish Football League combined.
For the purpose of this debate, ‘The Old Firm’ is offered to join the English Football league structure, entering initially in the English Premier League.

motion: THBT the IMF should declare China an intransigent creditor
This House Prefers a Common Law system over a Civil Law system
infoslide:
In Common Law systems (e.g. UK, US, India, New Zealand) judges interpret legislation within the context of specific cases and create new legal principles that form precedents for future rulings. Common Law systems are adversarial, such that lawyers of opposing parties advocate for a case, and judges act as a non-interventionist arbiter.
In a Civil Law system (e.g. France, Germany, Indonesia, Japan) laws are primarily codified in legislation by the government, leaving limited room for judicial interpretation. Civil Law systems are inquisitorial, such that while lawyers of opposing parties present the case, judges take a more active role in investigating the case, gathering evidence, and questioning witnesses.
Juries can exist in both systems.

motion: This House prefers Hayekian economic policies to Keynesian economic policies
infoslide:
Keynesian economics is a macroeconomic theory that emphasises the importance of strong government intervention (e.g. deficit spending, funding large infastructure projects, quantitative easing/tightening) to promote sustained growth.
Hayekian economics is a macroeconomic theory that emphasises the importance of limited government intervention (e.g. minimising annual deficits, free markets, constant monetary policy) to promote sustained growth.

motion: THBT Donald Trump winning the 2024 US Presidential Election is in the interest of the Chinese Communist Party
THBT left wing criticism of liberal NGOs for failing to be intersectional brings more harm than good
infoslide:
Recently, there has been a rise in left-wing criticism of liberal NGOs for failing to be intersectional.

Some examples include: the Guttmacher Institute, an abortion rights group, facing criticism for insufficient diversity in its workforce; and the American Civil Liberties Union, facing criticism for failing to prioritise free speech rights for specific minority groups.

motion: THBT it is in the interest of resource-rich nations (e.g. Serbia, Mexico and Argentina) to allow Western corporations to undertake mining operations for  the extraction of  'green minerals' (e.g. Lithium, Zinc, Nickel) that are essential for green technology.
THBT devolution has strengthened the Scottish independence movement
infoslide:
Devolution was the process of providing a regional government, and autonomy over defined policy areas, to Scotland and Wales in 1998.
Devolved powers are constrained to domestic issues (for example the Scottish and Welsh governments have control over their respective education systems, domestic transport infrastructure and health services). International issues are reserved to the central British Government (for example, trade deals, issues relating to security and defence).

motion: This House Predicts that Russia will not have control of most of the occupied and contested Ukrainian territories* by the end of the war
This House Hopes that the future of humanity is transhumanism
infoslide: Transhumanism refers to a future where advanced technologies are used to augment and transcend the biological limitations of humans (e.g. brain-computer interfaces, bionic implants, customizable genetic traits). It is meant to elevate human capabilities beyond their natural level, as opposed to medical uses of technology aimed at restoring basic capabilities (e.g. prosthetics for amputees, curing hereditary diseases).

motion: This House Believes That the EU should create a specialized court responsible for investigating and prosecuting political corruption across its member states
This House Opposes the strategy of deficit financing by Liberal Democracies
infoslide: Deficit financing is a deliberate voluntary strategy used by governments to finance their budget deficits or shortfalls in revenue by borrowing money rather than reducing expenditures or increasing taxes, in order to achieve specific economic and social objectives.

motion: This House Prefers a world without the desire for revenge
This House Opposes the commercialization of sex*
This House Opposes the rapid development of AI
This House Believes That aggressive power projection* in South East Asia is in China's interest
This House Prefers drug regulatory bodies (e.g. FDA, EMA, MHRA) to only evaluate whether pharmaceuticals (e.g. treatments, medicines, vaccines) are safe, but not whether they are effective
This House Opposes the use of political messaging in Children's Entertainemnt
infoslide:
In children's entertainment, a political message specifically addresses issues, policies, or power dynamics related to governance and public affairs. It aims to shape public opinion, influence political decisions, or promote specific political ideologies. Examples of children's media with political messages include "The Lorax," "Zootopia," and "Pocahontas"
It should not be confused with apolitical moral messages, which focus on teaching universal values like honesty, kindness, and empathy, and are prevalent in most children's media (e.g. "SpongeBob SquarePants," "Dora the Explorer," and "The Powerpuff Girls.").
The key distinction that makes a message political lies in whether the message primarily addresses specific political issues as compared to broader ethical principles.

motion: This House Would only provide state pensions to those mentally or physically unable to work
This House Predicts that the Judicial Reform will lead to Netanyahu's Exit from Office
infoslide: The Israeli Judicial Reform led by the Netanyahu government seeks to curb the judiciary's influence over lawmaking and public policy by limiting the Supreme Court's power to exercise judicial review and granting the government control over judicial appointments

motion: This House Would grant substantial authority to eSports Player Unions, including but not limited to, influence over tournament format, in-game balance, and working conditions
This House Believes That news publications should be anonymized and signed as a collective editorial
That we regret the decline of Sufism in the Indian subcontinent
infoslide: Sufism is a mystical tradition within Islam, emphasising the veneration of saints and their shrines. These shrines have been typically administered by hereditary custodians and are important sites of worship, culture and community life.

motion: That we oppose the adoption of Māori cuisine by elite culinary institutions
That we prefer to be born into a society with high-context norms over one with low-context norms
infoslide: High-context societies rely heavily on norms of shared history and relationships, non-verbal cues, and implicit meanings. Low-context societies rely heavily on norms of explicit, direct verbal communication where the words carry the bulk of the message.

motion: That we oppose Malaysia's attempts to resettle the Bajau
infoslide:
The Bajau are a group of Indigenous seas people traditionally found across the waters of Southeast Asia, especially in parts of the Philippines, Malaysia, and Indonesia. They are often known as 'sea nomads' because many Bajau communities historically live much of their lives on boats or in stilt houses above shallow coastal waters.
Malaysia's attempts to resettle the Bajau (Sama-Bajau) primarily involve state-led resettlement programs to the mainland or other coastal communities.

motion: That we oppose ethnographic refusal
infoslide: Ethnographic refusal is a methodological approach in anthropology where researchers deliberately choose not to collect, record, or disclose certain information about the communities they study. Examples of information typically withheld include burial or mourning practices, migration patterns, traditional medicines, etc.

motion: That humanity should voluntarily adopt the last generation policy
infoslide:
For the purposes of this debate, under the 'last generation' policy, humanity would collectively commit to ending reproduction. The current generation would become the final generation of humans.
A giant asteroid as big as the sun is approaching Earth and will not miss. It’s 100 years until doomsday, and humanity has been informed of this by their leaders.

motion: That Gongzhou should vote in favour of abandoning Earth’s charter
infoslide:
For the purposes of this debate, 'Gongzhou' is Earth's first planetary colony outside the solar system, set up by a limited number of humans. It has reached self-sufficiency.
On Gongzhou, a vote emerges: whether to continue obeying Earth’s charter (which prioritises research and return missions), or to dissolve the charter and reorganise into a fully independent political entity focused entirely on local survival and expansion.

motion: That Earth's first settlement mission to another habitable planet should be a generation ship rather than a cryogenic mission
infoslide:
A generation ship is a self-sustaining spacecraft where generations of humans are born, live, and die during journeys lasting hundreds of years. It has systems and institutions needed to sustain human life, facilitate reproduction, and allow for recreation.
Cryogenic missions instead freeze the crew in suspended animation to sleep through the entire voyage. They cannot be woken up until they reach their destination.
The year is 2100, and Earth has successfully developed the technological capabilities to carry out both.

motion: That we support the 'One Army' plan in Syria
infoslide: Under the Al Sharaa government's 'One Army' plan, all independent militias (including the US-backed SDF) are required to surrender their weapons, dissolve their militias, and integrate into a unified national military under central government command. In exchange, individual fighters may receive amnesty for any crimes committed during the civil war and either return to civilian life or integrate into the official security forces under the Ministry of Defense or Ministry of Interior. Militias which refuse to integrate will be disbanded and disarmed.

motion: That Turkey's decision to close the Bosporus and Dardanelles to warships since 2022 has been in Russia's interest
That we regret the rise of e-carceration
infoslide:
E-carceration is the use of digital technologies by the state to monitor and restrict the movement of people outside traditional prisons or jails. Examples include GPS ankle monitors that track location, smartphone supervision apps, and biometric check-ins at automated kiosks.

An AI Pause is an agreement whereby parties agree to cease the development of further AI capabilities. Parties may continue to engage in AI safety research, or work on improving existing AI models. The Big Five AI labs are Anthropic, Google, Meta, Open AI and SpaceX. It is estimated that the Big Five companies have approximately a two year lead in AGI development.

motion: That we believe that Benjamin Netanyahu will be the next Prime Minister of Israel
That California should abolish Riparian and Appropriative water rights and instead charge market rates to all water users
infoslide: California provides two main types of water rights. Riparian water rights entitle the owner of land adjacent to a water source to a share of the natural flow of water. Appropriative water rights allow the owner of land not adjacent to a water source to divert water for use. Appropriative water rights follow a 'first in time, first in right' system allowing the oldest rights holders priority over other users. Holders of both types of water rights pay a usage fee approximately twenty times lower than that of municipal water rates. Of the share of Californian water used by humans, 80% is used for agricultural purposes.

motion: That it is in the interests of liberals in the USA to advocate for greater state autonomy (e.g. lower federal taxation and higher state taxation, greater autonomy for state governments on labour and environmental laws)
That we should grant dictators amnesty in exchange for them stepping down
That developing countries should ban members of political dynasties from standing for political office
That we believe regimes accused of committing human rights violations should be investigated by Truth and Reconciliation  Commissions, rather than being subject to punitive mechanisms
That we support the Independent Forfeiture Act
infoslide: Sweden’s Independent Forfeiture Act allows the government to seize luxury goods from an individual, where such goods are disproportionate to the income of the individual, and the individual cannot provide a legitimate explanation for how they acquired the goods. The law does not require that the individual be charged with or suspected of a crime. The law applies to those under the age of criminal responsibility (15) in Sweden. A court must approve the seizure.

motion: That we should abolish the offence of concealing a serious indictable offence
infoslide: In New South Wales, it is an offence, called 'concealing a serious indictable offence' to fail to report a serious indictable offence, or to fail to provide any information that could assist police in relation to the serious indictable offence. The sentence for this offence is up to five years in prison. A 'serious indictable offence' is any offence which carries a sentence of at least five years in prison. Defences to concealing a serious indictable offence include having a reasonable excuse or being under 18.

motion: That we prefer career judiciary systems, to those where judges are appointed late in their life
infoslide:
Career judiciary systems (e.g. France, Germany, Japan, and South Korea) typically recruit judges early in their careers through competitive examinations and specialized judicial training programs.
By contrast, common-law jurisdictions (e.g. The United Kingdom, United States, Canada, and Australia) generally appoint judges after substantial experience as practicing lawyers, advocates, academics, or public officials.

motion: That we oppose Rafizi Ramli and Nik Nazmi's decision to break away from PKR and lead BERSAMA
infoslide: In May 2026, influential reformist politician Rafizi Ramli, and long time Anwar Ibrahim loyalist Nik Nazmi, resigned from their positions in PKR, the main party in the ruling coalition led by Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim. Together, they have rebranded and now co-lead what was formerly an existing but idle political party, BERSAMA. BERSAMA positions itself as a centre-left party focused on social welfare, political renewal, and youth engagement.

motion: That we regret the ALP tax reform package
infoslide:
As part of the 2026-2027 Federal Budget, the Australian Labor Party (ALP) proposed substantial tax changes including:
1. A minimum 30% tax on capital gains and trust distributions.
2. An end to the 50% capital gains discount, with the substitution of cost base indexation.
3. An end to negative gearing (allowing landlords to deduct net losses from their rental properties against their income tax), with the exception of newly built property (although existing negatively geared properties are exempt from these changes until they are transferred to a new owner).

motion: That we oppose Andy Burnham's promise to retain Labour's prior budget guardrails
infoslide:
Sir Keir Starmer's Government committed to two key budget guardrails:
1. No increases in Income Tax, VAT or National Insurance.
2. Public debt as a percentage of GDP will be lower than the current levels at the end of a rolling 5 year window.

motion: That the deployment of tripwire forces in disputed territories in the South China Sea is in the interest of the United States
infoslide: Tripwire forces are small numbers of troops deployed by a powerful protecting state inside the territory of an ally or partner state that is vulnerable to attack. Their purpose is to ensure that any attack on that ally will automatically involve the protecting state.

motion: That we oppose the ‘unwilling or unable’ doctrine
infoslide:
The ‘Unwilling or Unable’ doctrine is an international law principle allowing a state to use force against non-state actors (e.g. terrorist groups, militias etc.) on another state's territory without that state’s consent. This doctrine would broaden the scope of Article 51 of the UN Charter, allowing a state to take military action where a host state cannot, or refuses to, neutralise a threat. Prominent examples of the use of this doctrine include US action against ISIS in Syria, Colombian action against FARC in Ecuador, and Western intervention against Al-Qaeda in Pakistan and Yemen.

The Porcupine Strategy is a form of asymmetric defence; where a weaker state attempts to make invasion too costly for a belligerent. The Porcupine Strategy involves using large numbers of cheap and mobile weapons (e.g. mines, drones, shoulder launched anti-tank missiles, truck-launched anti-air or anti-ship missiles etc.) instead of traditional military equipment (e.g. fighter jets, battleships or tanks).

motion: That we believe that the decline of geographically concentrated red light districts in India (Kamathipura, Sonagachi, etc.) has not been in the interests of sex workers

That as an Australian Aboriginal or Torres Strait Islander novelist, we would write about Aboriginal or Torres Strait Islander experiences within modern Australian cities rather than life within traditional communities
That the Australia Group should adopt a binding export-control regime
infoslide: The Australia Group is an informal, non-binding export-control arrangement of 42 countries and the European Union, which advises on national licensing rules for dual-use biotechnology. Dual-use biotechnology refers to biological materials, equipment, techniques, software, or knowledge (e.g. disease samples, CRISPR, bioreactors) that has both civilian (medical, agricultural, etc) and military applications. Under a binding export-control regime, exporters would need government approval before transferring controlled dual use biotechnology to any country, including other members of the Group. States would decide whether to approve exports by assessing the recipient, their intended use, and the risk of misuse.

motion: That we support the Australian government aggressively growing its domestic refinement and production of rare earth minerals
infoslide: As of 2025, Australia has the fourth-largest reserves of rare earth minerals in the world (approximately 5 per cent of global reserves), and is also the fourth-largest producer of rare-earths (around 8 per cent of global production). Australia does not have significant facilities for processing raw rare earth mineral ores, and exports the raw ores to China.

motion: That we oppose the NCMP scheme
infoslide: Under the Non-Constituency Member of Parliament (NCMP) Scheme, Singapore guarantees the presence of at least twelve opposition members in their Parliament. Where fewer than twelve opposition members win a constituency election, the losing opposition candidates with the highest vote share (Best Losers) are invited to join Parliament as Non-Constituency Members of Parliament (NCMPs). NCMPs retain all the powers and responsibilities of regular MPs, but do not represent any particular constituency and receive a much smaller salary.

motion: That we oppose the removal of these benefits for conscripts
infoslide: Traditionally, many businesses in South Korea counted conscripts' time in service for promotions. This year, a judicial decision has banned this practice, on the basis that this practice is discriminatory.

motion: That in countries with bicameral legislatures, we prefer the equal contribution system to the equal representation system
infoslide: In bicameral legislatures, upper houses have the power to veto, amend, or delay legislation. Under an equal representation system, each state has an equal number of representatives in the upper house. Under an equal contribution system, each state has representation in the upper house proportional to their net tax contribution to the federal government.

motion: That we prefer a world where everyone had an average amount of empathy
That we regret the rise of 'self-crit' culture
infoslide: Self-crit' culture refers to a culture where individuals are encouraged to publicly and openly criticise themselves for their shortcomings.

motion: That we regret the Griner-Bout prisoner exchange
infoslide: In August 2022 Brittney Griner, a WNBA Champion and American Olympic Athlete, was convicted and jailed by Russian authorities on charges of possession and smuggling of cannabis. In 2008, Russian arms dealer Viktor Bout was arrested in Thailand, before being transferred to the US where he was sentenced to 25 years in prison on terrorism offences. In December 2022 the US and Russian governments agreed to a 1-for-1 prisoner exchange of Griner and Bout.

motion: That we regret the Bosman Ruling
infoslide:
The Bosman ruling was a major 1995 European Court of Justice (ECJ) ruling on the employment rights of football players. The decision had two major consequences:
1. Players were no longer tied to their club once their contracts ended, and as such clubs were no longer entitled to transfer fees when players left.
2. The abolition of the 3+2 rule, which limited teams to 3 foreign players and 2 naturalised players.

This House Prefers a World with the Eru Iluvatar
infoslide: The Eru Iluvatar is recently created machine which can be used on one animal at a time, to elevate its cognitive abilities to human-level sapience. The process permanently changes the animal, giving it reasoning, language, self-awareness, complex communication, and the ability to understand abstract concepts such as morality, identity, and purpose.

motion: This House, as Syria, Would pursue strong ties with Russia
This House Would not live a pious life
infoslide:
In Calvinism, the doctrine of predestination holds that God determines each person's fate at the moment of creation, with humanity separated into two groups: the elect, whom God has predestined for Heaven, and the reprobate, whom God has predestined for eternal punishment in Hell.
The elect are understood to live pious and virtuous lives, while the reprobate live sinful lives. It is believed that these behaviours are consequences of God's prior determination of their fate.
For the purposes of this debate, you are a 20-year-old who was raised in a Calvinist family and is entirely convinced of the doctrine of predestination. You do not know whether you are among the elect or the reprobate.

motion: This House Believes That the 2026 Israel-Lebanon Trilateral Framework is in the best interest of Lebanon
infoslide: The 2026 Israel-Lebanon Trilateral Framework is a proposed security arrangement involving Israel, Lebanon, and the United States aimed at reducing tensions along the Israel-Lebanon border. The framework seeks to increase the role of the Lebanese Armed Forces in southern Lebanon through ‘Pilot Zones’, where Lebanese forces would gradually take responsibility for security and monitoring. The disarmament of non-state actors in designated southern ‘Pilot Zones’ serves as the core condition for a phased, conditional Israeli military withdrawal and the restoration of state authority. The framework also includes mechanisms for coordination and oversight designed to reduce military activity by actors outside the Lebanese state.

motion: This House Believes That history should be taught using temporal relativism rather than presentism
infoslide: Presentism is the practice of applying contemporary moral standards when judging the past. Temporal relativism is the practice of applying the moral standards of the relevant historical period when judging the past.

motion: This House, as the Democratic National Committee, prefers that the 2028 Democratic Presidential Nominee is a moderate rather than a progressive
This House Regrets 'Feminist Exceptionalism'
infoslide:
For the purpose of this debate, 'Feminist Exceptionalism' is the belief that women should strive to be extraordinary, high-achieving, or break glass ceilings.

motion: This House, as Barisan Nasional, Would abandon Pakatan Harapan in favour of a coalition with Perikatan Nasional for the 2028 Malaysian General Elections
infoslide: Pakatan Harapan is a reformist, multiracial coalition led by Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim, serving as the largest constituent of the current unity government. It focuses heavily on progressive governance and anti-corruption. However, it faces intense pressure from voters over inflation and economic reforms. Barisan Nasional is the traditional, Malay-nationalist coalition, that ruled Malaysia for 60 years until 2018. Led by UMNO, it acts as a complex partner in the federal unity government with Pakatan Harapan. It frequently clashes with Pakatan Harapan locally, to regain its lost voter base. Perikatan Nasional is the more conservative, Malay-Muslim opposition coalition, anchored by Bersatu and the Islamist party PAS. It rides a powerful wave of conservative voter sentiment. This makes it the primary threat to the current government in rural and Malay-majority areas.

motion: This House Opposes birthright citizenship

This House Believes That governments in agricultural-industrial dual economies should prioritise affordable food for consumers over policies that increase or stabilise the prices received by domestic farmers
infoslide: An agricultural-industrial dual economy is one in which a large, traditional, labour-intensive agricultural sector, exists alongside a substantially more productive, capital-intensive, industrial sector. Examples include India and Nigeria. Governments in these countries often employ policies to keep consumer food prices low (e.g., removing tariffs on agricultural imports, restricting agricultural exports) or to increase farm-gate prices (e.g., high agricultural tariffs, import quotas, guaranteed government purchasing).

motion: This House Opposes the relaxation of index inclusion rules
infoslide: Stock indexes (e.g., S&P500 and Dow Jones) traditionally impose certain requirements on firms before they can be included in an index, even if they are sufficiently large enough to qualify. These requirements might include profitability, liquidity, length of time as a public company, and governance structure. Some indexes have suggested relaxing some or all of these requirements to allow for faster entry of large technology companies that have or will soon have Initial Public Offerings (e.g., SpaceX, OpenAI, Anthropic, etc.)

motion: This House Would mandate that state-funded Vietnamese art initiatives prioritise digital adaptation over strict historical preservation
infoslide:
Digital adaptation means using modern technology to present Vietnam’s cultural heritage. Examples include 3D scanning, virtual reality, digitising water puppet shows, digital archives, and virtual tours of historical sites such as Huế. These techniques can be used to recreate historical buildings, artworks, or cultural objects in a modern digital form.
Historical preservation means protecting Vietnam’s historical and cultural heritage for future generations. Examples include restoring Hội An, conserving Mỹ Sơn Sanctuary, protecting traditional artworks, preserving Vietnamese art techniques and maintaining historical buildings in Huế.
